verses.note: The land promise defines the space in which Abram's descendants are to live as God's people. Its borders are repeated to Moses and Joshua (Deuteronomy 1:7, Joshua 1:4), and Israel's history returns to it again and again.
From this point ‘Israel’ is both a man and, soon, a people (verse 32). The nation's identity is rooted in this night: a people named for wrestling with God and surviving by his blessing.
The nation carries its ancestor's wound in its daily life. A meal becomes a small act of memory that Israel's identity began with a man who was blessed and lamed by God on the same night.

The social distance Egypt keeps from the Hebrews helps preserve Jacob's family as a distinct people. Separation that looks like contempt becomes part of how God keeps the family intact until it becomes a nation.
The name Israel marks Jacob as the bearer of the promise at the moment he decides to take the family to Egypt. The descent that begins here will end with a nation brought out in the exodus.
